# Video Trimmer

- Route: `/tools/video-trimmer`
- Kind: `tool`
- Category: `video`
- Slug: `video-trimmer`

## Summary

Cut a clip to the part you want with a fast, quality-preserving trim — no re-encode when possible. (Video tools)

## Details

Trimming keeps one stretch of a video and discards the rest. Most online trimmers re-encode the whole clip to do that, which is slow and costs quality. This page does something simpler by default: it asks FFmpeg to seek to your start time and copy the compressed video and audio packets to a new file for the requested duration, without decoding them. That is a stream copy, it is lossless, and it runs about as fast as the file can be read. If the copy cannot work, because the source codec is not allowed in the container you chose, or because you ticked the frame-accurate option, the server re-encodes just the selected stretch instead.
### What it does
- Cuts a single range out of a video, from a start time to an end time, typed in seconds or picked on a visual timeline.
- Copies the streams without re-encoding whenever the output container accepts the source codecs, so the kept part is bit-for-bit the original.
- Falls back automatically to a re-encode when the copy is refused, and lets you force a re-encode for a cut on the exact frame.
- Writes MP4 by default, or MOV or WebM; MP4 and MOV get the faststart flag so playback starts before the download finishes.
- Checks with ffprobe that the file actually has a video stream and refuses audio-only uploads with a clear message.
### How to use it
1. Upload the video: MP4, MOV, M4V, WebM, MKV, AVI, FLV, WMV, MPEG or MPG, uploaded straight to our storage bucket.
2. Set start and end: Type the seconds or drag the two handles; the panel shows the resulting clip length.
3. Pick a container and, if needed, frame accuracy: MP4 is preset. Tick Re-encode for a frame-accurate cut only when the exact frame matters.
4. FFmpeg cuts: A stream copy with -ss, -t and -c copy; or a libx264 CRF 18 re-encode when copying is impossible or you asked for it.
5. Download the clip: The output carries the _trimmed suffix and lives in the job folder until its retention window ends.
### Supported formats
- Input: mp4, mov, mkv, webm, avi, m4v
- Output: mp4, mov, webm
- Stream-copy when possible (no quality loss); re-encode fallback uses H.264 + AAC for MP4.
### Technical details
- The stream-copy command is ffmpeg -ss START -i input -t DURATION -map 0 -c copy -avoid_negative_ts make_zero [-movflags +faststart] output (runTrimVideo in specialized_tools.go). -map 0 keeps every stream, including extra audio tracks and subtitles, and times are written with millisecond precision.
- With -ss placed before -i and no decoding, FFmpeg can only begin at a keyframe, so the copy starts at the nearest keyframe at or before your start time. On a phone recording keyframes are typically 1 to 2 seconds apart, which is the most the beginning can drift; -avoid_negative_ts make_zero then rebases the timestamps so players start cleanly.
- The re-encode path uses buildVideoCodecArgs at the high quality setting: libx264 -crf 18 -pix_fmt yuv420p with AAC for MP4 and MOV, or libvpx-vp9 -b:v 0 -crf 18 with Opus for WebM. Only the first video stream and the first audio stream (if any) are mapped, so extra tracks are dropped on this path.
- Copy mode is sent as auto, which tries the copy and re-encodes on failure. Choosing WebM for an H.264 source always ends up on the re-encode path, because WebM only accepts VP8, VP9 and AV1 video.
- Validation on the server: start must be 0 or later, the clip must be at least 0.1 seconds long and at most 6 hours, and end must be after start. Anything else is rejected before FFmpeg starts and the operation is refunded.
- Because trimming is a specialized mode, the upload skips the automated content analysis that standard conversions receive; the server only runs ffprobe and the cut.
### When not to use it
Do not use the trimmer to remove several separate sections from one video; it keeps exactly one range, so a middle cut needs two trims and a join in Darkroom. Do not expect a stream copy to land on the exact frame; if a cut that is a second early matters, tick the re-encode option and accept a short encode. If your real goal is a smaller file, trimming only helps as much as you cut; the compressor changes the bitrate. And if the upload has no video stream, for example an M4A renamed to MP4, the trimmer refuses it; the audio tools handle audio-only files.
### Use cases
- Meeting and lecture recordings: Drop the minutes of people joining before the content begins.
- Highlights for social posts: Keep the 20 seconds that matter and upload only those.
- Evidence and bug reports: Share exactly the moment a problem happened, with the original quality intact.
- Preparing a GIF or a restoration snippet: Cut to a few seconds before feeding the clip to a tool that works best on short input.
### FAQ
Q: Does trimming re-encode my video?
A: Not by default. The server copies the compressed streams with -c copy, so the kept part is identical to the original. It re-encodes only when you tick the frame-accurate option or when the container you chose cannot hold the source codec, as with WebM for an H.264 file.
Q: Why does my clip start a moment before the time I typed?
A: A stream copy can only begin at a keyframe, and FFmpeg picks the nearest one at or before your start time. Keyframes are usually 1 to 2 seconds apart on camera footage. Tick Re-encode for a frame-accurate cut to start on the exact frame.
Q: Which output containers can I choose, and which keep the original quality?
A: MP4, MOV and WebM. MP4 and MOV accept the H.264 or HEVC video and AAC audio most cameras produce, so they stay lossless. WebM only accepts VP8, VP9 and AV1, so an H.264 source is re-encoded to VP9 at CRF 18 for that choice.
Q: How long or short can the trimmed clip be?
A: At least 0.1 seconds and at most 6 hours, with the end after the start. Daily limits and file caps depend on the plan; quote them only from the live plan block.
Q: Does it keep all the audio tracks and subtitles?
A: In the stream-copy path yes: -map 0 copies every stream in the file. In the re-encode path only the first video and first audio stream are kept.
Q: Can I trim a video to multiple parts at once?
A: No. One upload produces one clip from one range. For several pieces, run the trimmer once per range, or assemble the parts on a timeline in Darkroom.

## Routing

When to send a visitor here: Send visitors here when they want to keep one part of a video, for example "cut the first ten seconds", "keep just 1:20 to 2:05" or "shorten this clip". It cuts a single start-to-end range, without re-encoding when possible.
When to send them elsewhere: Removing several separate sections, or cutting out a middle part, needs Darkroom (content-studio). A smaller file without cutting content belongs in Compress Video (compress-video), and audio-only files go to Trim Audio (trim-audio).
Related tools: compress-video (shrink the kept clip); content-studio (multiple cuts and joins); trim-audio (trim an audio file); convert-video-to-animated-gif (turn the cut into a GIF); extract-audio-from-video (keep only the sound)
